items.title: Inverting a multiplicative set of nonzerodivisors does not change the total ring of fractions
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that inverting a multiplicative subset S of R made of nonzerodivisors does not change the total ring of fractions, Q(R) being isomorphic to Q(S^{-1}R), and that consequently Q(R) agrees with Q(Q(R)) (statement lines 4809-4815). The proof isolates the one step that could fail, namely the passage from a nonzerodivisor of S^{-1}R to its numerator: if x = r/f with f in S is a nonzerodivisor, then r must be a nonzerodivisor in R, and this is exactly what the hypothesis on S is for (proof lines 4817-4820). The author leaves the assembly of the two rings of fractions to the reader once that step is in hand. H2.
